title: Print each office's staff list in the order its readers expect

blocks.text: Each of the company's offices prints its staff list from one server. Readers complain: in London `bram` comes after `Mira`, in Paris `Élodie` comes after `Gustav`, and the Stockholm office says its list is in "German order". Last month a reorder also dropped three people from a list because their names matched a colleague's, or differed from it only in case or accents.

Finish `sortForDisplay(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/StaffDirectory.java`: every name, in the order a reader in the office's locale expects. The server's default locale is not the office's. About three lines in total.

cases.says: capitalised names without accents come out in alphabetical order
a name written in lowercase sorts among the names with the same first letter, not after all capitalised names
a name starting with an accented capital sorts with its base letter, not after Z
names that differ only in case or accents are all on the list, and so are two people with the same name
the order follows the office's locale, not the server's default: Swedish files Ö after Z, German with O

origin.section: compareTo Orders UTF-16 Units; People Need a Collator, and Its 0 Merges Set Entries

concepts: A sorted set treats its comparator's 0 as a duplicate, so a collator at PRIMARY strength drops names that differ only in case or accents.
compareTo orders by UTF-16 unit, so capitals come before lowercase and accented capitals after z; CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER fixes case only; a Collator for an explicit locale orders for people.
